message.content: {"baseline":{"title":"Why Do Vision LLMs Struggle with Spatial Awareness and Object Placement in Images?","body":"An archived Reddit post from 2025 discusses how vision-capable LLMs like ChatGPT, Grok, and Gemma 3 27B seem to capture only a general concept of images rather than detailed spatial information. The author wonders if these models rely on a vision transformer that extracts limited information, or if the image is fully loaded into memory for detailed analysis, or if a separate perceptron provides just a structured list of detected objects. Notably, when asked to recreate images with accurate object placement and scale (e.g., using JavaScript Canvas), these LLMs fail to position objects correctly, indicating a lack of real spatial awareness. The author would consider it a success if the models could at least output bounding boxes with correct positions and sizes, but this appears beyond their current capability. Given these observations, what technical approaches might vision LLMs be using internally that lead to this limitation?
